cases.title: Search that stops one short
cases.briefMd: Return the index of `target` in the sorted array `nums`, or `-1` if it isn't there.
choices: The loop stops while one candidate is still left: it should run while `lo <= hi`.
Computing `mid` from `lo + hi` can overflow, so `mid` is sometimes wrong.
When `nums[mid] < target` it should move `hi`, not `lo`.
It should return `lo` instead of `-1` when the target is missing.
cases.explanationMd: `hi` starts at the last index, so the search range is inclusive: `[lo, hi]`. With `lo < hi` the loop exits when exactly one element is left, without ever looking at it. Searching for 5 in `[5]` compares nothing and returns -1, and the last element of a range can be skipped, e.g. 3 in `[1, 3]`. Inclusive bounds need `while lo <= hi`.

cases.title: A number that pairs with itself
cases.briefMd: Return the indices `[i, j]` (`i < j`) of two different elements of `nums` that add up to `target`, or `[]` if there are none.
choices: It records each number before looking for its partner, so a number can pair with itself.
A hash map can't find the partner in O(1); the array has to be sorted first.
It should look up `target + x`, not `target - x`.
It returns the two indices in the wrong order.
cases.explanationMd: The map should only hold numbers *before* index `i`. Here `x` is stored first, so when `target - x == x` the lookup finds `x` itself and returns `[i, i]`: with `[3, 2, 4]` and target 6 it answers `[0, 0]` instead of `[1, 2]`. Check for the partner first, then record the number.

cases.title: The best sum is never negative
cases.briefMd: Return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray of `nums`.
choices: `best` starts at 0, so an all-negative array reports 0, a sum no subarray has.
`cur` should drop to 0 whenever it goes negative instead of becoming `x`.
It only considers subarrays that start at index 0.
`max(x, cur + x)` should be `min(x, cur + x)`.
cases.explanationMd: The subarray must be non-empty, so the answer can be negative. Starting `best` at 0 acts like an empty subarray worth 0: for `[-3, -1, -2]` it returns 0 instead of -1. Start `best` at `nums[0]` (or negative infinity).

cases.title: Brackets left open
cases.briefMd: Return whether `s` (only `()[]{}` characters) is balanced: every bracket closes in the right order.
choices: Opening brackets still on the stack at the end are never checked, so `"(("` counts as balanced.
It should push closing brackets and pop on opening ones.
Checking for an empty stack before popping rejects valid strings.
It fails on nested pairs such as `"([])"`.
cases.explanationMd: Every closing bracket is matched correctly, but nothing checks for openers that never got closed. `"(("` pushes twice, never pops, and the function returns true. The answer is "balanced" only if the stack is empty at the end.

cases.title: Merging in the order given
cases.briefMd: Merge all overlapping intervals (touching ones like `[1,4]` and `[4,5]` count) and return them sorted by start.
choices: The intervals are never sorted by start, so overlapping ones that aren't next to each other stay apart.
`start <= last end` should be `start < last end`: touching intervals must stay separate.
It should keep `min` of the two ends, not `max`.
It needs a second pass to merge chains of three or more intervals.
cases.explanationMd: The one-pass merge only works if each interval can only overlap the one just before it, which is true once they are sorted by start. Unsorted, `[[8,10],[1,3],[2,6]]` keeps `[8,10]` first and never merges correctly. Sort by start first (O(n log n)), then sweep.

cases.title: Buying yesterday
cases.briefMd: `prices[i]` is a stock's price on day `i`. Return the best profit from buying on one day and selling on a later day (0 if no profit is possible).

similarLC.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

choices: It compares each price with the day before instead of with the lowest price so far.
`low` has to be updated before the profit is computed.
`best` should start at `prices[0]`.
It should walk from the last day backwards to find the highest price first.
cases.explanationMd: `low` tracks the cheapest day so far, but the profit line ignores it and uses `prices[i - 1]`, which only finds the best *one-day* rise. For `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` it answers 1 instead of 4. Selling today is best paired with the lowest earlier price: `prices[i] - low`.

cases.title: A window that slides back
cases.briefMd: Return the length of the longest substring of `s` with no repeated characters.
cases.explanationMd: When `ch` was seen before, the window must start after that earlier copy, but only if that copy is still inside the window. Without `max`, `left` can jump backwards: in `"abba"`, the second `a` moves `left` back to 1 and the window `"bba"` (length 3) is counted. `left = max(left, last[ch] + 1)` keeps the window moving forward only.

cases.title: Moving the wrong wall
cases.briefMd: `height[i]` is a wall at position `i`. Return the most water two walls can hold: `(j - i) * min(height[i], height[j])`.
cases.explanationMd: The area is limited by the shorter wall. Moving the taller wall inward can never help (the width shrinks and the height is still capped by the short wall), so the two-pointer scan must move the **shorter** side. These two lines are swapped: it moves `r` when the left wall is shorter, and `l` otherwise.

cases.title: One place too early
cases.briefMd: `nums` is sorted with distinct values. Return the index of `target`, or the index where it would be inserted to keep `nums` sorted.
cases.explanationMd: When the loop ends without finding `target`, `lo` and `hi` have crossed: `hi` is the last element smaller than `target` and `lo = hi + 1` is the first larger one, which is exactly where `target` belongs. Returning `hi` is one too early (and -1 for a target smaller than everything).

cases.title: The first slot never sees the right side
cases.briefMd: Return an array where element `i` is the product of every element of `nums` except `nums[i]`, without using division.
cases.explanationMd: The first pass stores the product of everything left of `i`; the second pass must multiply in the product of everything right of `i` for **every** index, including 0. The loop stops at 1, so `res[0]` keeps 1 instead of the product of the rest: `[1, 2, 3, 4]` gives `[1, 12, 8, 6]`.

cases.title: Skipping the bottom
cases.briefMd: `nums` was sorted ascending (distinct values) and then rotated, e.g. `[3, 4, 5, 1, 2]`. Return its minimum in O(log n).

similarLC.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

cases.explanationMd: If `nums[mid] <= nums[hi]`, the right half is sorted, so the minimum is at `mid` or to its left. `mid` itself may be the minimum, so it must stay in range: `hi = mid`. With `hi = mid - 1`, `[3, 1, 2]` throws away the 1 and answers 3.

cases.title: A set that stays empty
cases.briefMd: Return whether any value appears at least twice in `nums`.
cases.explanationMd: The set is the memory of values already seen. Without adding each value after checking it, the set stays empty and the function always answers false. One pass with a hash set is O(n) time and O(n) space.

cases.title: An island that never sinks
cases.briefMd: `grid` holds 1 (land) and 0 (water). Return the number of islands: groups of land cells connected up, down, left or right.
cases.explanationMd: `sink` has to mark each land cell as visited before exploring its neighbours, here by turning it into water. Without that, two neighbouring land cells keep calling each other forever and the recursion overflows the stack. Marking also makes sure each island is counted once.

cases.title: Stairs that only count up by one
cases.briefMd: You climb `n` stairs taking 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.
cases.explanationMd: The ways to reach step `i` are the ways to reach `i - 1` plus the ways to reach `i - 2`, so two running values `a` (two steps back) and `b` (one step back) shift forward each step: the new `b` is `a + b` and the new `a` is the old `b`. Without the shift the count only grows by one at a time.
